newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada to host Japan-Peru talks on hostage crisis.
newsitem.headline: Canada to host Japan-Peru talks on hostage crisis.

text.p: Prime Minister Jean Chretien confirmed on Wednesday Canada would host a meeting between Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori and Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on the Lima hostage crisis.
The meeting on Saturday in Toronto would "discuss ways to resolve the ongoing hostage-taking in Lima," Chretien said in a statement.

Leftist Tupac Amaru rebels crashed a party at the Japanese ambassador's residence on Dec. 17, taking more than 500 hostages. All but 72 have been released, but the crisis has now been dragging on with little sign of resolution.
Hashimoto said in Tokyo that Fujimori, who is of Japanese descent, told him that he wanted to discuss the situation as soon as possible.
"Canada has been chosen for the site of this meeting because of its role as a member of the Commission of Guarantor and the convenience of its location for both leaders," Chretien's statement said.

The commission was set up by the Peruvian government and the guerrillas to serve as a forum for eventual negotiations. It met formally for the first time on Tuesday, although there were no negotiations to supervise.
The rebels are demanding the release of 400 jailed comrades -- a demand Peru has refused to discuss.

Ottawa's representative on the panel, Canadian Ambassador and former hostage Anthony Vincent, had won respect from all sides by serving initially as a mediator after being released early in the six-week crisis.

Chretien spokeswoman Leslie Swartman said she expected Vincent would come up from Peru for the talks. She was not sure if Chretien would go to Toronto, but pointed out the meetings will be between Fujimori and Hashimoto.
Fujimori, has taken a tough stance in dealing with the Tupac Amaru rebels -- even though his brother Pedro is one of the hostages.

Japan had initially taken a softer line but then backed Fujimori's position. This week, however, Hashimoto called for restraint by Peruvian forces who have been conducting shows of strength near the ambassador's residence.
"I'm worried if the terrorists have been irritated over moves of the special forces. We are asking for care to be taken about such moves," he told reporters in Tokyo on Tuesday.
